bib.title: Reinforcement Learning Teachers of Test Time Scaling

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Reinforcement Learning Teachers of Test Time Scaling", Edoardo Cetin, Tianyu Zhao, Yujin Tang (Sakana AI). NeurIPS 2025 (39th Conference). arXiv:2506.08388v3, dated 29 Oct 2025. The v1 appeared in June 2025 (the ID 2506 implies June). The PDF shows only the v3 date.
COVERAGE: 28 of 28 pages, 107,191 chars. All of the main text and appendices A-E were read. References (pp. 10-14) were skimmed. The appendix example traces (Figs 8-12) were skimmed only.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. A 7B RLT's raw traces, with no filtering or post-processing, give better students than distilling post-processed traces from far larger teachers (R1 671B, QwQ-32B, Gemini Flash Thinking).
 number: 7B student 49.50 vs Bespoke (R1 traces) 46.60; 32B student 73.23 vs 71.47 (average of AIME24, MATH500 and GPQA Diamond).
 setup: 17K question-solution pairs from Li et al. Students are Qwen2.5-7B/32B-Instruct. The RLT is Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, with 1 sample per question. Single-sample accuracy. Baseline numbers are copied from prior work where available.
 quote: "RLT-7B (Ours) 17K 23.30 82.80 42.40 49.50" and "RLT-32B (Ours) 17K 66.70 93.40 59.60 73.23" (Table 1, p.6). Bespoke-7B 17K: 46.60, Bespoke-32B 17K: 71.47.
 where: p.6, Table 1.
2. At 1K samples the gap is bigger, and R1 traces degrade when subsampled.
 number: 7B-1K 47.43 vs 42.37; 32B-1K 71.37 vs Bespoke-32B-1K 65.60 and s1-32B 66.40.
 quote: "RLT-32B-1K (Ours) 60.00 94.00 60.10 71.37" (p.6).
 where: p.6.
3. Cost: the RLT is orders of magnitude cheaper than R1. The authors call it a lower-bound estimate of R1's cost, not a measurement.
 number: R1 training >688,000 H800 GPU-hours and data generation >1,067 H100 hours. RLT 280.4 H100 hours to train and 6.7 to generate.
 quote: "7B RLT teacher 280.4 (H100) 6.7 (H100)" (Table 4, p.15). Also: "while distilling a 32B student on fixed traces took less than a day on a single H100 compute node, training this larger model using RL on the same questions would have taken months with the same hardware." (p.10)
 where: p.15 (A.3), p.10.
 Caveat: the R1 figure is a "large approximation". It was built from the 2,048 H800 count and public statements, and it ignores multi-generation, filtering and post-processing costs. It also counts R1's whole RL run, not only trace generation.
4. Cold-starting RL (Table 2, p.7). The RLT-7B cold start followed by RL beats the Bespoke (R1 traces) cold start. A 7B teacher trained with ordinary RL gives a worse cold start.
 number: RLT-7B + RL 50.53 vs Bespoke-7B + RL 48.30 vs "RL no cold-start" 40.77. Raw traces from a 7B RL teacher gave 38.60, which is below the base model's 39.17. With GPT-4.1-mini post-processing they gave 43.93.
 setup: RL phase is one epoch on the LIMR set (<1K problems, 86 steps, batch 1024).
 quote: "RLT-7B + RL (Ours) 17K 26.70 84.00 40.90 50.53"
 Note: on GPQA, Bespoke-7B + RL (45.40) beats RLT-7B + RL (40.90).
5. Zero-shot transfer to Countdown (p.8-9). RLT traces generated on a new task without retraining the RLT give students that beat direct RL on that task.
 number: "50.8 vs. 49.2" is direct RL vs students distilled from the original math set. The text says RLT distillation "achieves even higher performance than direct RL" (the values are only in the Figure 4 bar plot). Direct RL and Bespoke-7B share a >98.5% overlap in solved problems.
 setup: 16K train and 1K test Countdown problems, generated automatically.
 quote: "stark overlap of over 98.5% in the final sets of solved problems between direct RL and the RL-free Bespoke-7B baseline" (p.9).
6. Reward ablation (Table 14, p.24). The KL term is essential. Without it the teacher copies the solution tokens and the student drops below the base model.
 number: full 49.50; no KL term 34.10 (base 39.17); no min/max reduction 47.43. Without min/max, think-token length "almost doubles" and training is slower. The 47.43 student still beats the R1 baseline's 46.60.
7. The reward predicts distillation quality (Sec 4.5, p.9). 16 datasets were built by reward rank from the pre-RL RLT, and 16 students were trained.
 number: Pearson over 0.89. The best-ranked pre-RL traces already give 90% of the R1 pipeline's gains.
 quote: "with a Pearson coefficient over 0.89" and "already yield 90% the performance gains of our baseline R1 distillation pipeline".
8. Teacher size (Table 11, p.22). A 3B RLT is worse, and most of the gap shows up with a 32B student.
 number: 3B teacher: 7B student 46.50, 32B student 63.90, against 49.50 and 73.20 for the 7B teacher. This is a small gain over the Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct base at 53.20. Table 11 shows 46.7 on AIME for the 3B teacher against 66.7 for the 7B teacher.
9. Student side and algorithm (Tables 10, 12).
 number: RLOO gives 48.80 vs 49.50 for GRPO. A 7B+32B student ensemble for the reward gives 49.70. A 2-stage run, where the student is re-distilled midway, gives 50.70.
10. Extra benchmarks (Table 9, p.21). The 7B RLT is slightly behind Bespoke on LCB-Average (34.63 vs 36.10), and ahead on OlympiadBench, with a higher overall score.
 number: Overall 40.37 vs 39.70 at 7B. 67.62 vs 65.68 at 32B. LCB-Hard 32B 32.50 vs 26.20.
11. Data-scale check on NuminaMath (Table 13). RLT stays ahead of R1 traces at 1K and 10K. On 1K NuminaMath the gap is small, and the RLT beats the Bespoke 1K NuminaMath baseline by only 45.80 vs 43.00.

Method (for notes):
- The RLT gets question and solution in its prompt and writes an "explanation" that becomes the think trace.
- Reward is r = r_SS - λ·r_KL. r_SS is the student's avg and min log-prob of the solution given the question and the explanation. r_KL is the KL between the teacher (which sees the solution) and the student (which does not), over the think tokens.
- λ=3, α=0.01. Trained with GRPO, 125 steps, batch 1024, group 64, lr 1e-6, context 16384. This is less than one epoch, preceded by a short SFT on Bespoke open data. The reward student is Bespoke-Stratos-7B.
- Seeds: single run, single sample per eval. No error bars or seeds are reported. I searched for them and found none. Small differences such as 49.5 vs 48.8 are therefore weak evidence.

LIMITS
- It needs ground-truth solutions. Without them it must fall back on larger models.
- It is not pure RL. It needs an SFT warm start on pre-collected reasoning traces, and it needs a student model to compute the reward (the authors say training time is more than 90% generation).
- It never solves problems from scratch, so it does not replace the RL-for-reasoning step for the final capability. It provides traces only.
- 16384 context cap, 7B teachers only, no scaling beyond that. They did not test broader question corpora, or teacher and student trained jointly or as the same model.
- Eval is math, science, coding and Olympiad only. Baselines were mostly copied from prior papers, and the R1 comparison uses different teacher post-processing pipelines. Bespoke-7B-1K was newly run.
- The cost estimate for R1 is a rough lower bound (see claim 3).
- Dated: Qwen2.5 / R1 / Bespoke-era baselines (early 2025).

BUILDS ON: Guo et al. 2025 (DeepSeek-R1, GRPO); Shao et al. 2024 (DeepSeekMath, GRPO); Muennighoff et al. 2025 (s1); Li et al. 2025 (Sky-T1 and "structure, not content" LLMs Can Easily Learn to Reason from Demonstrations); Bespoke Labs 2025 (Bespoke-Stratos); Yue et al. 2025 (does RL expand reasoning beyond the base model); Ahmadian et al. 2024 (RLOO); Li, Zou, Liu 2025 (LIMR); Shen et al. 2025 (Satori); NovaSky 2025 (Sky-T1).

WHICH NOTE: It bears most on 08-reasoning-rl-deepseek-r1.md ("distillation of reasoning"): the claim that distilling R1-style traces beats RL on small models, and that cold-starting from distilled traces helps. The "which teacher" question in 05-post-training-for-agents.md also fits: a small specialised teacher with the answer in context beats a big RL'd reasoner at distillation. It supports the framing in 01 only weakly (sparse versus dense reward and exploration).

QUOTES
1. "In practice, the raw outputs of a 7B RLT provide higher final performance on competition and graduate-level tasks than existing distillation and cold-starting pipelines that collect and postprocess the reasoning traces of orders of magnitude larger LMs." (p.1, abstract)
2. "Unlike for correctness-based rewards, our learning signal is inherently dense, providing informative rankings to the RLT's output even before achieving any task expertise." (p.6)
3. "while distilling a 32B student on fixed traces took less than a day on a single H100 compute node, training this larger model using RL on the same questions would have taken months with the same hardware." (p.10)

FIGURES: Fig 1 (p.1) is a bar summary of RLT vs larger-LM distillation at same-size and 32B students. Fig 2 (p.3) contrasts the RL format with the RLT format. Fig 3 (p.4) shows how teacher tokens go into the student format for the reward. Fig 4 (p.8) has the Countdown transfer and the reward-rank correlation. Figs 8-12 (pp.23-26) show think-token lengths and ablation traces. I did not run the figure script.

PROBLEMS: None serious. Equations are garbled in the extraction. No embedded instructions found. Tables 1-14 were extracted cleanly.
